title: Risk-banded rollback advisor for SLO-driven canaries
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Implement a production-safe, explainable rollback advisor that uses risk bands (green/amber/red) derived from multi-signal SLOs — latency (p95/p99), error-rate, token cost per request, and throughput — to trigger graduated automated responses during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts. The advisor should be cohort-aware (traffic slices by region, customer tier, request length), offer tunable hysteresis/hold windows, and expose a simulation API so PMs and SREs can validate rollback policies against historical traffic and synthetic probes.

Novel aspects compared to prior work: instead of hard static thresholds, we compute dynamic risk bands using cohort baselines + quantile drift detection and a Bayesian confidence band over delta (candidate vs baseline). Rollback actions are graduated: alert only, throttle traffic, divert to fallback model, and full rollback. Each action has a minimum evidence window and cost-weighted veto. Also integrate token-cost signal so the advisor can prevent deployments that cause regressions in inference unit economics even if latency SLOs remain within bounds.

Scope: backend service + small console UI for policy tuning, rollout simulation, and policy change audit logs. Integrations: Redwood Console alerts, rollout engine (canary traffic controller), and Console dashboards for per-route breakdown. Deliverables: API endpoint for advisor decisions, a simulation harness CLI, rollout policy schema extension, and a console policy editor preview with explainability traces.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor returns one of {OK, THROTTLE, DIVERT, ROLLBACK} within 200ms for a canary decision endpoint under 99th percentile traffic
Risk bands computed per-cohort and persisted for audit with explainability trace (metric deltas + posterior confidence) visible in Console
Simulation harness can replay 90 days of historical traffic and show advisor decisions with an accuracy (>90%) vs offline oracle defined by hand-labeled incidents
Policy UI allows SRE/PM to tune hysteresis (min-evidence-window), cost veto threshold, and cohort scope and save versioned policies
comments: 2026-03-06 — Aisha Khan: Kickoff meeting notes attached in links. We agreed on Bayesian delta + quantile baselining as primary signal fusion approach. Action: ENG to prototype estimator using canary replay dataset.

2026-03-08 — Liam Chen: Prototype implemented: cohort baselines for p95/p99 latency and token-cost-per-request. Initial results: in quantized model test, p95 latency increased 22% for long-tail (seq>1024) cohort; token cost dropped 15% but overall cost per productive token increased due to higher retry rate. Saved as replay run #23 (link).

2026-03-10 — Priya Desai (SRE): Reviewed prototype. Concern: transient spikes during GC-like events lead to false positives. Decision: require consecutive evidence windows (configurable default 3) and add synthetic probing to validate persistent regressions.

2026-03-11 — Design review (Jules Park): Console mockups accepted with minor changes — show confidence band, primary contributing signals, and recommended action with rationale. Jules requested an option to 'simulate with current live traffic' before applying policies to active rollouts.

2026-03-12 — Security (Maya Ortiz): No additional data access required beyond existing telemetry. Audit logging requirement noted for policy changes. Scheduled security signoff as part of release checklist.

2026-03-13 — Liam Chen: Open PR created for advisor service (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124). Seeking reviewers from 1) serving-runtime (for metric instrumentation hooks) and 2) console (for policy UI integration).
next_steps: Merge PR for advisor core service; wire metric exporters for token-cost per route; implement simulation CLI; build Console policy editor draft; schedule canary of advisor on non-critical internal route for 2 weeks of observation.
